source.title: MaxVA: Fast Adaptation of Step Sizes by Maximizing Observed Variance of Gradients
source.authors: Chenfei Zhu; Yu Cheng; Zhe Gan; Furong Huang; Jing-Jing Liu; T. Goldstein

record.file_problem: Full paper text supplied, including appendices; minor extraction/formatting artifacts do not prevent reading.
record.tranche_reason: Tests adaptive-optimizer comparisons on image classification and language tasks, including pretrained and large-batch settings. It reports held-out performance but does not measure the generalization gap as defined in the claim versions.
record.gate_note: Rows cover the paper's own image-classification test-accuracy comparisons and held-out benchmark results where optimizer effects are measured. Training loss and test scores for BERT pretraining are included because the text compares test performance across optimizers. Synthetic optimizer convergence results and other metrics that do not measure a listed version are omitted.
record.test_reason: The paper's own ResNet18 experiments compare adaptive optimizers with SGD on held-out image accuracy and therefore test V4. Training-test gaps are not required for that comparison. It does not test V5: batch size is never varied under a comparable training budget.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is broadly accurate. The authors conclude that MaxVA adapts second-moment averaging to gradient variance, improves stability and convergence, and yields strong empirical performance. They report improved downstream BERT scores over Adam and LAMB and a reduced image-classification accuracy deficit relative to SGD, rather than universal superiority to SGD. Their convergence proof covers the zero-momentum case under stated assumptions.
record.recipe_differences: The paper introduces MaxVA and compares MAdam/LaMAdam with established optimizers; it does not reproduce the cited original studies' interventions. It reports selected optimizer benchmarks rather than measuring train-test generalization gaps.
record.method_sensitivity: Outcomes differ by dataset and optimizer: adaptive methods are near SGD on CIFAR-10, below it on CIFAR-100 and ImageNet, and MAdam/LaMAdam are reported to improve on Adam for the listed GLUE tasks. The BERT run uses two batch sizes across two pretraining phases, but no batch-size contrast is tested.

fits_no_version.finding: MAdam and LaMAdam improve GLUE development scores over their corresponding adaptive baselines.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Changing adaptive second-moment averaging can improve pretrained Transformer fine-tuning performance relative to other adaptive optimizers.

fits_no_version.finding: At the same large-batch BERT schedule, MAdam reaches lower training loss and higher downstream scores than Adam and LAMB.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Optimizer choice affects convergence and downstream performance at a fixed large-batch pretraining schedule.

fits_no_version.finding: Appendix D reports poor translation BLEU for AdaBound's recommended clipping schedule and much better BLEU when clipping is effectively inactive.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: AdaBound's transition toward SGD can harm Transformer translation performance relative to effectively retaining Adam; this is not a direct test of switching from Adam to SGD.

record.problems: The paper does not report train-test gaps in the cited benchmark results. ImageNet has no reported uncertainty and fewer runs than CIFAR; the authors state they could not complete 4 runs per hyperparameter there. The BERT comparison has no small-batch control and its main training-loss comparison is not a generalization measure. Several comparator figures are cited from prior work.
record.rows_left_out: No separate rows for synthetic-data convergence curves (Sections 4.1–4.2, Figures 2–3, 7): these measure optimization loss/update behavior rather than the listed claim versions. Figure 4 training-loss traces are omitted because the tabulated GLUE dev metrics provide the optimizer comparison. Machine-translation BLEU rows (Table 2) omitted because the claim versions concern image-classification generalization and the paper does not report training-test gaps there.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting versus natural-label held-out performance.
Width sweeps beyond the width needed for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected architectures and local connectivity.

The exact learning-rate-and-schedule-only tuning condition; these image experiments also tune decoupled weight decay and use AMSGrad on CIFAR. No controlled limited-versus-broader tuning comparison, coupled-versus-decoupled decay ablation, direct Adam-to-SGD switch, word-level language-model comparison, or image training-performance comparison is reported.
All batch-size effects on held-out performance: no comparable small-batch control, fixed-epoch batch sweep, or controlled recovery of a measured batch penalty.
Dropout ablations, training-set-size dependence, and removal with weight decay.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its correlation with generalization gaps.
Removing memorized examples versus equally many random examples.

record.verdict_notes: Only supplied text was used. This study is not an original source for V4. Its weight-decay tuning, decoupled decay, and CIFAR AMSGrad materially qualify comparisons with V4's limited-tuning clause. Adaptive-only benchmarks do not independently test adaptive-versus-SGD generalization. No omitted result requires a V1–V8 row.

versions.untested_parts: No random-label memorization or natural-label generalization comparison.
No network-width sweep or interpolation-threshold analysis.
No convolutional versus fully connected architecture comparison.

Does not test the cited limited-tuning comparison across the broader benchmark set or whether broader tuning reverses it. It tests several adaptive methods against SGD and compares Adam-family methods in selected settings.
No controlled batch-size comparison or fixed-epoch comparison; only large-batch BERT pretraining with optimizer comparisons.
No dropout ablation or dropout-by-training-set-size comparison.
No removal of memorized training examples.

relationships.condition: ResNet18 on CIFAR-100: Adam and LaProp with AMSGrad, with learning rate and decoupled weight decay tuned
relationships.reason: R7–R9 show SGD at 79.62% versus Adam at 78.77% and LaProp at 78.36%, retaining the adaptive-method disadvantage even under this expanded recipe.
relationships.display_finding: The reported lower accuracies for Adam and LaProp than SGD after learning-rate and decoupled-weight-decay tuning remain unverified.

relationships.condition: ResNet18 on CIFAR-100: proposed MaxVA adaptive optimizers
relationships.reason: R7, R11 and R12 show that MAdam and LaMAdam reduce the adaptive-method deficit to 0.30 and 0.41 points, while remaining below SGD.
relationships.display_finding: Reported MAdam and LaMAdam deficits of 0.30 and 0.41 percentage points relative to SGD remain unverified.

relationships.condition: ResNet18 on CIFAR-10: tuned adaptive methods with AMSGrad
relationships.reason: R1–R3 and R5–R6 show only 0.06–0.10-point deficits for three adaptive methods and a marginal 0.07-point advantage for MAdam; a substantial adaptive penalty does not appear.
relationships.display_finding: Reported small deficits for three adaptive methods and a marginal MAdam advantage remain unverified.

relationships.condition: ResNet18 on ImageNet: LaProp and MAdam with tuned decoupled weight decay
relationships.reason: R13, R15 and R17 show small remaining deficits of 0.16 and 0.22 points against SGD, with no reported uncertainty.
relationships.display_finding: Reported LaProp and MAdam deficits of 0.16 and 0.22 percentage points remain unverified and lack uncertainty estimates.

relationships.condition: ResNet18 on ImageNet: LaMAdam with tuned decoupled weight decay
relationships.reason: R13 and R18 show 70.18% for SGD and 70.16% for LaMAdam, which the authors describe as nearly matching SGD under the adapted recipe.
relationships.display_finding: Reported LaMAdam accuracy of 70.16% versus SGD's 70.18% remains unverified.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: ResNet18 image classification on CIFAR-100 and ImageNet
reader_labels.reason: Adam-family methods are below the SGD test-accuracy comparator in several reported settings; see R8–R9, R11–R12, R15, R17–R18. The paper itself says adaptive methods often underperform carefully tuned SGD on these datasets.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: ResNet18 image classification on CIFAR-10 with MAdam
reader_labels.reason: MAdam's reported CIFAR-10 test accuracy is above the SGD comparator; see R1 and R5.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: RoBERTa-base fine-tuning on the 8 reported GLUE dev tasks
reader_labels.reason: MAdam and LaMAdam show a mixed and generally modest difference from Adam, with the authors reporting better scores for these methods; see R19, R21, R22.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.reason: MAdam's reported downstream test scores exceed Adam and Lamb, but there is no small-batch comparison, so the fixed-epoch large-batch penalty is not established; see R26–R31.
